questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why did Europeans search for a sea route to India?

options.A: To spread Christianity only
options.B: To gain direct access to the lucrative Asian trade in spices and textiles and reduce dependence on intermediaries
options.C: To establish political rule over India

questions.explanation: Europeans sought direct access to the lucrative Asian trade in spices, textiles and other goods, to reduce dependence on intermediaries and secure commercial and strategic advantages.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which developments encouraged European overseas expansion from the fifteenth century?

options.A: Improvements in navigation, shipbuilding, cartography and maritime technology, along with state-sponsored exploration
options.D: The decline of the Mughal Empire

questions.explanation: Improvements in navigation, shipbuilding, cartography and maritime technology, together with state-sponsored exploration and competition for trade, encouraged European expansion from the fifteenth century.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who reached India by the sea route around the Cape of Good Hope in 1498?

options.A: Christopher Columbus

questions.explanation: The Portuguese navigator Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast in May 1498.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Where did Vasco da Gama land in India in 1498?

options.A: Goa

questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar Coast in May 1498.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the ruler of Calicut when Vasco da Gama arrived?

options.A: The Zamorin (Samudiri)

questions.explanation: The ruler was the Zamorin (Samudiri) of Calicut, a title used by the rulers of that port kingdom.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which European power was the first to establish a durable maritime empire in India?

options.A: The English

questions.explanation: The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish a durable maritime and fortified trading presence in the Indian Ocean region after Vasco da Gama's voyage.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which European trading companies later competed in India alongside the Portuguese?

options.A: English, Dutch, French and Danish

questions.explanation: The English, Dutch, French and Danish established trading companies or settlements in India, alongside the earlier Portuguese presence.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was a 'factory' in the context of European trade in India?

options.A: An industrial manufacturing plant
options.B: A trading station or commercial establishment where company agents stored goods and conducted business

questions.explanation: A factory was a trading station or commercial establishment where company agents stored goods, conducted business and coordinated exports; it did not necessarily mean an industrial manufacturing plant.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the first Portuguese governor in India?

options.A: Afonso de Albuquerque

questions.explanation: Francisco de Almeida became the first Portuguese governor or viceroy in India in 1505.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Blue Water Policy?

options.A: A policy of extensive territorial conquest inland
options.B: Francisco de Almeida's policy emphasising naval supremacy and control of sea routes rather than territorial conquest
options.C: A policy of alliance with Indian rulers

questions.explanation: Francisco de Almeida's Blue Water Policy emphasised naval supremacy and control of sea routes rather than extensive territorial conquest inland.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who established the Portuguese Estado da India at Goa?

options.A: Francisco de Almeida

questions.explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 from the Bijapur Sultanate and made it the principal centre of Portuguese power in the East.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: From which kingdom did Afonso de Albuquerque capture Goa in 1510?

options.A: Vijayanagara

questions.explanation: Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 from the Bijapur Sultanate.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why was Goa important to the Portuguese?

options.A: It was a religious pilgrimage site
options.B: It became the administrative, naval, commercial and religious centre of the Portuguese Estado da India
options.C: It was the capital of the Mughal Empire
options.D: It was a centre of spice production

questions.explanation: Goa became the administrative, naval, commercial and religious centre of the Portuguese Estado da India.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Cartaz system?

options.A: A Portuguese naval pass or permit system imposed on merchant shipping in the Indian Ocean

questions.explanation: The Cartaz system was a Portuguese naval pass or permit system imposed on merchant shipping in parts of the Indian Ocean. Ships without the required pass could be seized or attacked.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which of the following was an important Portuguese settlement in India?

options.A: Pulicat

questions.explanation: Important Portuguese centres included Goa, Daman, Diu, Bassein (Vasai), Chaul, Cochin (Kochi) and parts of the Konkan and Malabar coasts.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which crops or plants are associated with Portuguese introduction or spread in India?

options.A: Rice, wheat and barley
options.B: Chilli, tobacco, cashew, pineapple, papaya and maize

questions.explanation: Portuguese maritime networks helped introduce or popularise crops from the Americas and elsewhere, including chilli, tobacco, cashew, pineapple, papaya and maize.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Where and when was the first printing press in India established?

options.A: Goa in 1556 by the Portuguese

questions.explanation: The first printing press in India was established by the Portuguese at Goa in 1556.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Portuguese contribution to Indian naval trade?

options.A: They developed fortified coastal bases, naval patrols, customs controls and the Cartaz pass system

questions.explanation: They developed fortified coastal bases, naval patrols, customs controls and the Cartaz pass system to influence Indian Ocean trade.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Why did Portuguese power decline in India?

options.A: Competition from the Dutch and English, limited resources, administrative weaknesses, changing trade patterns and stronger European naval companies
options.B: The Portuguese never had any power in India
options.C: They were defeated by the Mughals

questions.explanation: Portuguese power declined because of competition from the Dutch and English, limited resources, administrative weaknesses, changing trade patterns and the rise of stronger European naval companies.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When did India take control of Goa, Daman and Diu from the Portuguese?
questions.explanation: India took control of Goa, Daman and Diu in December 1961 through Operation Vijay, ending Portuguese colonial rule there.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Dutch East India Company (VOC) established?
questions.explanation: The Dutch East India Company, or VOC (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie), was established in 1602 by the Dutch Republic.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the main aim of the Dutch in Asia?

options.A: Territorial conquest of India
options.B: Control of the profitable spice trade and commercial networks across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia

questions.explanation: The Dutch primarily sought control of the profitable spice trade and established commercial networks across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which was the principal Dutch centre on the Coromandel Coast?

options.A: Cochin

questions.explanation: Pulicat, north of present-day Chennai, was an important early Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel Coast.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which of the following was an important Dutch settlement in India?

options.A: Pondicherry

questions.explanation: Important Dutch settlements included Pulicat, Nagapattinam, Cochin, Chinsurah, Kasimbazar, Patna, Balasore and Surat at different times.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What commodities did the Dutch trade in India?

options.A: Textiles, indigo, saltpetre, opium and other commodities

questions.explanation: The Dutch traded in textiles, indigo, saltpetre, opium and other commodities, using Indian textiles in exchange networks across Southeast Asia.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which battle weakened Dutch ambitions in Bengal?

options.A: Battle of Plassey

questions.explanation: The Battle of Chinsurah or Biderra in 1759, in which the English defeated Dutch forces, weakened Dutch military ambitions in Bengal.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the French East India Company established?
questions.explanation: The French East India Company was established in 1664 under the initiative of Jean-Baptiste Colbert during the reign of Louis XIV.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the French governor associated with the expansion of French power in India?

options.A: Joseph Francois Dupleix

questions.explanation: Joseph Francois Dupleix was the French governor-general in India who pursued an ambitious policy of political intervention and influence in the Carnatic and Deccan.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which was the principal French settlement in India?

options.A: Chandernagore

questions.explanation: Pondicherry (Puducherry) became the principal French settlement and administrative centre in India.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Name an important French settlement in India.

options.A: Pulicat

questions.explanation: Important French settlements included Pondicherry, Chandernagore, Mahe, Karaikal and Yanam.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What were the Carnatic Wars?

options.A: A series of three conflicts fought mainly between the English and French East India Companies and their Indian allies in the Carnatic and Deccan between 1746 and 1763
options.B: Wars between the Mughals and Marathas
options.C: Wars between the British and Mysore
options.D: Wars between the Portuguese and Dutch

questions.explanation: The Carnatic Wars were a series of three conflicts fought mainly between the English and French East India Companies and their Indian allies in the Carnatic and Deccan between 1746 and 1763.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the First Carnatic War fought?
questions.explanation: The First Carnatic War lasted from 1746 to 1748 and was connected to the War of the Austrian Succession in Europe.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which treaty ended the First Carnatic War and returned Madras to the English?

options.A: Treaty of Paris

questions.explanation: The French captured Madras in 1746 and returned it under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the significance of the Battle of St. Thome or Adyar (1746)?

options.A: A small French force defeated a much larger force of the Nawab of Carnatic, demonstrating the military effectiveness of disciplined European-style infantry and artillery
options.C: It established British supremacy in India

questions.explanation: In 1746, a small French force defeated a much larger force of the Nawab of Carnatic near the Adyar River, demonstrating the military effectiveness of disciplined European-style infantry and artillery.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Second Carnatic War fought?
questions.explanation: The Second Carnatic War lasted approximately from 1749 to 1754 and involved rival claimants to the thrones of Hyderabad and Carnatic, backed by the French and English respectively.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Robert Clive?

options.A: A French governor
options.B: An English East India Company officer who played a major role in the Company's military and political expansion

questions.explanation: Robert Clive was an English East India Company officer who played a major role in the Company's military and political expansion, especially in Bengal and the Carnatic.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the significance of the capture of Arcot (1751)?

options.A: It strengthened the English position and damaged French-backed claims in the Carnatic
options.B: It ended the French presence in India

questions.explanation: Robert Clive captured and defended Arcot in 1751 during the Second Carnatic War, strengthening the English position and damaging French-backed claims in the Carnatic.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Third Carnatic War fought?
questions.explanation: The Third Carnatic War was fought from 1756 to 1763 as part of the global Seven Years' War.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which battle ended French political ambitions in India?

options.A: Battle of Plassey

questions.explanation: The Battle of Wandiwash (Vandavasi) in 1760 was a decisive English victory over the French under Count de Lally, severely weakening French political ambitions in India.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Treaty of Paris of 1763 in relation to India?

options.A: It ended the Seven Years' War; France recovered certain trading settlements but was restricted from maintaining them as major fortified political-military bases
options.B: It gave France control of Bengal
options.C: It ended French presence in India completely
options.D: It established British rule over France

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Paris of 1763 ended the Seven Years' War. France recovered certain trading settlements in India but was restricted from maintaining them as major fortified political-military bases.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Did the French completely leave India after 1763?

options.A: Yes, they left immediately
options.B: No, French settlements continued but political and military influence was greatly reduced; remaining territories were transferred to India in 1954 (de facto) and 1962 (de jure)
options.C: Yes, they were expelled by the British
options.D: No, they established a new empire in India

questions.explanation: No. French settlements continued, but French political and military influence was greatly reduced. The remaining French territories were transferred de facto to India in 1954 and de jure in 1962.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: When was the English East India Company established?

options.A: 31 December 1600

questions.explanation: The English East India Company was established by royal charter of Queen Elizabeth I on 31 December 1600.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was the original purpose of the English East India Company?

options.A: To conduct English trade with the East Indies and Asian markets
options.B: To establish political rule in India

questions.explanation: It was formed to conduct English trade with the East Indies and Asian markets, initially focusing on spices and later expanding into Indian textiles and other commodities.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Who was the first Englishman to visit the Mughal court as an ambassador of the Company?

options.A: Sir Thomas Roe

questions.explanation: Captain William Hawkins reached Jahangir's court in 1609, seeking trading privileges.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Who obtained important trading privileges from Jahangir for the English?

options.A: Captain William Hawkins

questions.explanation: Sir Thomas Roe, ambassador of King James I, visited Jahangir's court from 1615 to 1619 and secured privileges that helped the Company expand its trade.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Where was the first English factory in India established?

options.A: Surat in 1613

questions.explanation: The English established an early factory at Surat in 1613 after receiving Mughal permission; earlier commercial attempts and temporary establishments had also occurred.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Which English settlement became the Company's first major base in eastern India?

options.A: Surat
options.C: Hugli in Bengal (factory established in 1651), followed by the growth of Calcutta

questions.explanation: The Company established a factory at Hugli in Bengal in 1651, followed by the growth of Calcutta as a major settlement.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: How did Bombay come under English control?

options.A: It was captured in battle
options.B: It was transferred to the English Crown as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza when she married Charles II in 1661; the Crown leased it to the East India Company in 1668
options.C: It was purchased from the Portuguese
options.D: It was gifted by the Mughal emperor

questions.explanation: Bombay was transferred to the English Crown as part of the dowry of Catherine of Braganza when she married Charles II in 1661; the Crown leased it to the East India Company in 1668.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: How did Madras become an English settlement?

options.A: The Company acquired land from local rulers and established Fort St. George at Madras in 1639-1640
options.B: It was captured from the French
options.C: It was purchased from the Dutch
options.D: It was gifted by the Nawab of Carnatic

questions.explanation: The Company acquired land from local rulers and established Fort St. George at Madras in 1639-1640, which became a major English centre on the Coromandel Coast.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What were the three major British Presidency towns in India?

options.A: Delhi, Agra and Lahore

questions.explanation: The three major Presidency towns were Madras, Bombay and Calcutta, each serving as an important administrative, military and commercial centre.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was the Regulating Act of 1773?

options.A: The first major British parliamentary intervention to regulate the East India Company's administration in India; it made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta
options.B: An act that ended the Company's monopoly
options.C: An act that transferred power to the Crown

questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first major British parliamentary intervention to regulate the East India Company's administration in India. It made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of Bengal?

options.A: Lord William Bentinck

questions.explanation: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal in 1773 under the Regulating Act.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: When did the Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta, begin functioning?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act provided for a Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta, which began functioning in 1774.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was Pitt's India Act of 1784?

options.A: It established a system of dual control: the Company retained commercial and some administrative functions, while the British government exercised political supervision through the Board of Control
options.D: It created the office of Viceroy

questions.explanation: Pitt's India Act of 1784 established a system of dual control: the Company retained commercial and some administrative functions, while the British government exercised political supervision through the Board of Control.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was the Charter Act of 1813?

options.A: It ended the Company's monopoly over Indian trade, except for trade in tea and trade with China, and provided for an annual sum to support education in India
options.B: It ended the Company's commercial activities entirely
options.C: It transferred power to the Crown

questions.explanation: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly over Indian trade, except for trade in tea and trade with China, and provided for an annual sum to support education in India.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was the Charter Act of 1833?

options.A: It ended the Company's commercial activities, made it primarily an administrative body, designated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India and centralised legislative authority
options.C: It created the Board of Control

questions.explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's commercial activities, made it primarily an administrative body, designated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India and centralised legislative authority.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: Who was the first Governor-General of India?

options.A: Warren Hastings

questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India under the Charter Act of 1833.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: What was the Charter Act of 1853?

options.A: It separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council more clearly and opened the way for recruitment to the civil services through competitive examination
options.D: It created the office of Secretary of State

questions.explanation: The Charter Act of 1853 separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council more clearly and opened the way for recruitment to the civil services through competitive examination.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.chapter: British Arrival and East India Company
questions.question: When did the East India Company lose its rule in India?
questions.explanation: The East India Company's rule ended in 1858 after the Revolt of 1857, when the Government of India Act transferred governance to the British Crown.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Battle of Plassey fought?

options.A: 23 June 1757

questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between the East India Company forces led by Robert Clive and the forces of Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was the Nawab of Bengal defeated at the Battle of Plassey?

options.A: Mir Qasim

questions.explanation: Siraj-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of Bengal who opposed the growing power of the East India Company and was defeated at Plassey in 1757.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who conspired with the English during the Battle of Plassey and was installed as Nawab of Bengal?

options.A: Mir Qasim

questions.explanation: Mir Jafar was a commander who conspired with the English during the Battle of Plassey and was installed as Nawab of Bengal after Siraj-ud-Daulah's defeat.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the significance of the Battle of Plassey?

options.A: It gave the East India Company decisive political influence in Bengal and access to its wealth, helping finance further military expansion
options.B: It ended British rule in India
options.C: It established French power in Bengal

questions.explanation: Plassey gave the East India Company decisive political influence in Bengal and access to its wealth, helping finance further military expansion.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When was the Battle of Buxar fought?

options.A: 23 June 1757

questions.explanation: The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 between the Company forces under Hector Munro and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who led the Company forces at the Battle of Buxar?

options.A: Robert Clive

questions.explanation: The Battle of Buxar was fought between the Company forces under Hector Munro and the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Treaty of Allahabad of 1765?

options.A: Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa
options.C: It established French rule in India

questions.explanation: Under the Treaty of Allahabad, Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa in 1765, giving it the right to collect revenue.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What did Diwani rights mean?

options.A: The rights to collect revenue and administer civil financial matters in a territory
options.B: The right to rule a princely state
options.D: The right to maintain an army

questions.explanation: Diwani rights were the rights to collect revenue and administer civil financial matters in a territory. The Company's acquisition of these rights gave it a major source of income and political power.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who introduced the Dual Government in Bengal in 1765?

options.A: Warren Hastings

questions.explanation: Robert Clive introduced the Dual Government in Bengal in 1765. The Company controlled revenue collection while the Nawab nominally retained responsibility for administration.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who ended the Dual Government in Bengal in 1772?

options.A: Robert Clive

questions.explanation: Warren Hastings ended the Dual Government in 1772.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who introduced the Subsidiary Alliance system from 1798?

options.A: Lord Wellesley

questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley systematically expanded the Subsidiary Alliance policy from 1798 to bring Indian rulers under British control.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Subsidiary Alliance?

options.A: An Indian ruler accepted British troops and paid for their maintenance, usually surrendered control over foreign relations and accepted a British Resident
options.D: A military alliance against the French

questions.explanation: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, an Indian ruler accepted British troops and paid for their maintenance, usually surrendered control over foreign relations and accepted a British Resident. Failure to pay could lead to territorial cessions.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which Indian ruler first accepted a Subsidiary Alliance with the British in 1798?

options.A: Tipu Sultan

questions.explanation: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted a subsidiary alliance in 1798 under Lord Wellesley.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Doctrine of Lapse?

options.A: A policy under which the British annexed certain princely states when a ruler died without a natural male heir, refusing to recognise an adopted heir for succession to sovereignty
options.B: A policy of granting subsidies to rulers

questions.explanation: The Doctrine of Lapse was a policy associated with Governor-General Lord Dalhousie under which the British annexed certain princely states when a ruler died without a natural male heir, refusing to recognise an adopted heir for succession to sovereignty.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who introduced the Doctrine of Lapse?

options.A: Lord Wellesley

questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General from 1848 to 1856, is associated with the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which state was annexed in 1853 under the Doctrine of Lapse and is one of its best-known examples?

options.A: Awadh

questions.explanation: States annexed under the policy included Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur in central India (1852), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854). The best-known examples are Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Was Awadh annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?

options.A: Yes, in 1856
options.B: No, Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the stated grounds of alleged misgovernment, not under the Doctrine of Lapse

questions.explanation: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the stated grounds of alleged misgovernment, not under the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When were the four Anglo-Mysore Wars fought?
questions.explanation: The four Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought between Mysore and the British East India Company and its allies in 1767-1769, 1780-1784, 1790-1792 and 1799.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Hyder Ali?

options.A: A British governor
options.B: The effective ruler of Mysore in the mid-eighteenth century who modernised the army and fought the British

questions.explanation: Hyder Ali rose from military service to become the effective ruler of Mysore in the mid-eighteenth century. He modernised the army and fought the British in the Anglo-Mysore Wars.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Who was Tipu Sultan?

options.A: Son of Hyder Ali who ruled Mysore from 1782 to 1799 and resisted British expansion

questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan, son of Hyder Ali, ruled Mysore from 1782 to 1799. He resisted British expansion, pursued military and administrative reforms and was killed defending Srirangapatna in 1799.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Treaty of Mangalore?

options.A: Signed in 1784, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War and restoring captured territories and prisoners on terms of mutual restitution
options.B: Signed in 1792, ending the Third Anglo-Mysore War
options.D: Signed in 1799, ending the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Mangalore was signed in 1784, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War. It restored captured territories and prisoners between Mysore and the Company on terms of mutual restitution.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the Treaty of Seringapatam?

options.A: Signed in 1792 after the Third Anglo-Mysore War; Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territories and paid an indemnity
options.B: Signed in 1784 ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War
options.C: Signed in 1799 ending the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War

questions.explanation: The Treaty of Seringapatam was signed in 1792 after the Third Anglo-Mysore War. Tipu Sultan ceded about half his territories to the British and their allies and paid an indemnity.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When and where did Tipu Sultan die?

options.A: 4 May 1799 while defending Srirangapatna (Seringapatam)

questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan died on 4 May 1799 during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War while defending the fortress of Srirangapatna (Seringapatam) in Karnataka.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the result of the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?

options.A: The British-led forces captured Srirangapatna in 1799, Tipu Sultan was killed, and much of Mysore was redistributed; the Wadiyar dynasty was restored in a reduced princely state under British paramountcy
options.C: The French took control of Mysore

questions.explanation: The British-led forces captured Srirangapatna in 1799, Tipu Sultan was killed, and much of Mysore was redistributed among the victors. The Wadiyar dynasty was restored in a reduced princely state under British paramountcy.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: When were the three Anglo-Maratha Wars fought?
questions.explanation: The three Anglo-Maratha Wars were fought in 1775-1782, 1803-1805 and 1817-1818, ending the Peshwa's power and bringing major Maratha states under British paramountcy.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: Which treaty ended the First Anglo-Maratha War in 1782?

options.A: Treaty of Salbai

questions.explanation: The First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782) ended with the Treaty of Salbai in 1782, which restored a general peace and recognised Madhavrao II as Peshwa.

questions.subject: Indian History
questions.question: What was the outcome of the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803-1805)?

options.A: Major British victories over the Scindia and Bhonsle forces, expanding British influence in central and northern India
